what: InterContinental Hotels Group franchises and manages hotels rather than owning them. Its brands include Holiday Inn, Holiday Inn Express, Crowne Plaza, InterContinental, Kimpton and Six Senses, covering roughly a million rooms.
customers: Hotel owners who franchise its brands, and travellers who book through its system and loyalty programme.
money: a percentage of room revenue from franchised hotels
fees for running hotels owned by others
a handful of hotels it owns directly
moat: A booking system and loyalty programme with over 100 million members that fills rooms more cheaply than an independent hotel can, which is why owners pay for the brand.
risks: Travel demand falls in a recession and fees fall with it
Chinese hotel performance has been weak
Analyst targets imply the shares are above fair value
Debt of about $4.5 billion against under $1 billion of cash
opportunities: Return on invested capital of 58%, because it owns almost no property
Gross margin of 85% as the fees carry almost no cost
The room pipeline under development keeps growing without its own capital
watch: Revenue per available room, and net system size growth.
